title: 第四十五章 云州第四十四章 玄帝
slug: 纳玄尘第五十三章安凌
content_zh:
第四十五章云州
云州城的城墙在午后的光里显出灰扑扑的颜色，不算高，也不矮。城墙面上有些地方已经开裂了，缝隙里长出一丛丛枯草，在风里摇摇晃晃的。
城门前排着一列等着进城的人——有挑着担子的货郎，有赶着驴车的农户，还有几个牵着马的行商。三三两两地散着，堵在城门口慢慢往前挪。货郎的担子里装着些针线布头，农户的车上堆着几捆干柴，行商的马背上驮着鼓鼓囊囊的包袱。一个守城士兵蹲在一辆驴车旁边，翻了翻车上的柴捆，又摆了摆手让车过去。
苏尘牵着马排在队尾，等了一阵，总算轮到他了。
城门口守着四个士兵。一个坐在条凳上收进城费，两个站着看人，还有一个在翻看进城者的文书。轮到苏尘的时候，他把入城文书递了过去。
守城士兵接过来看了一眼——目光在文书边角的一处印记上停了一下，没说什么，把文书合上递还给他。
“劳驾稍等。“他说了一句，转身往城门洞里走了几步。
他跟旁边一个士兵低声说了句话。那士兵点了点头，快步往城里去了。
苏尘站在城门边上等了一会儿。身后的队伍还在慢慢地往前挪，有人探头看了他一眼，又缩了回去。没有人知道他在等什么。他靠在马鞍上，一只手搭着缰绳，目光落在城门洞里来来往往的人身上，脸上没什么表情。
没过多久，一个穿灰布短褐的中年人从城里快步走了出来。
他没有穿官服，看装扮像个管事，但走路利落，脚步又快又稳。目光在人群里一扫就锁定了苏尘——他没有犹豫，没有左顾右盼，像是早就知道苏尘长什么样、站在哪里。
他走过来，拱手低声说了一句：“公子跟我来。“
没有叫世子，没有多余的话，转身就在前面带路。
苏尘牵着马跟上了他。
两人穿过两条街。街上的人渐渐多了起来——一个挑着担子的小贩从他们身边挤过去，担子两头挂着竹篮，里面装着青菜和豆腐。有人在路边蹲着挑拣一堆山货，跟摊主讨价还价。一个小孩子追着一只狗跑过去，差点撞到苏尘的马。苏尘拉了一下缰绳，让马避了一下。
拐进一条安静的巷子，在一个侧门前停住了。那人叩了两下门，门从里面打开。他侧身让苏尘进去，然后自己留在门外，没有跟进来。
门内早有一个管家模样的人在等着。管家约莫五十来岁，穿着一身洗得发白的灰布长衫，头发梳得一丝不苟。他没有多说话，只是微微躬了一下身，然后领着苏尘穿过一条走廊，到了正厅门口。
没过多久，一个穿着青色官服的中年人从里面快步走了出来。
他约莫四十出头的年纪，面皮白净，下巴上留着打理整齐的短须。看见苏尘便笑着拱了拱手。
“在下许敬堂，云州司牧。你就是世子吧——王爷信里提过，我在门口候了一会儿了。“

他说着侧身让了一下：“快请进。“
苏尘也拱了手，叫了一声“司牧大人“，跟着他进了府。
正厅不大，但收拾得讲究。正对大门的墙上挂着一幅字——写的是“静水流深“四个字，笔力沉稳。两边摆着两排深木色的椅子，中间一张茶几，上面放着一套青瓷茶具。窗子开向南面，午后的光从窗外照进来，在地砖上投下一块明亮的方格子。
许敬堂把他领到主位坐下，亲自倒了茶，屏退了左右。
等脚步声远了，他才开口。
“王爷前几日派人飞书过来，说世子要南下天邑办差，会经云州落脚。“许敬堂笑了一下。“信上还说，让我照应着些。“
他端起茶碗喝了一口，目光落在苏尘身上。
“世子在云州打算停留几日？“
“歇一晚就走，明日一早继续赶路。“苏尘说。“不敢多叨扰司牧大人。“
“这有什么叨扰的。“许敬堂摆了摆手。“王爷难得开口让我办什么事，世子既然来了，就安心住下。府里地方宽敞，我让人备一间客房就是。“
苏尘顿了一下。
“谢司牧大人好意。“苏尘说。“不过府里往来人多，我住着也不自在。司牧大人若方便，在城里帮我安排一处清静的住处就行，不必太讲究。“
许敬堂看了他一眼，没有勉强，笑着点了一下头。
“那也行，东街有处空院子，平时没人住，我让人收拾一下，世子住那边吧。晚上若得空，过来吃顿便饭？“
苏尘应了一声好。
又坐了一会儿，许敬堂问了几句路上的情形——走了几天、路好不好走、沿途可还太平。又问了几句朔州的近况——王爷身体可好、王妃可安好、边关那边情形如何。都是些家常话，语气随意，像是在跟故人之子聊天。苏尘一一答了，话不多，但也不让人觉得疏远。
又说了几句闲话，苏尘便起身告辞了。
许敬堂让方才领路的那位管家送苏尘去了东街的院子。
院子不大，一进的格局，正屋两间，厢房一间。院子中间铺着青砖，角落里种着一棵枣树，叶子已经掉得差不多了。几片枯叶还挂在枝头上，风一吹就晃两下，但始终没有掉下来。树下的砖缝里长着几株瘦弱的杂草，已经干枯了，黄褐色的一小撮，蜷在墙角。
收拾得还算干净，被褥也是新换的。屋子里的家具不多，但该有的都有——一张床，一张桌子，一把椅子，墙角立着一个脸盆架。窗纸是新糊的，透进来的光线柔和而均匀。空气里有一股淡淡的皂角味，像是刚打扫过。

苏尘把行李放下，洗了把脸，在院子里站了一会儿。
枣树的枝桠在头顶上交织着，把灰白的天空切割成细碎的小块。风从院子口灌进来，带着街上传来的隐隐约约的人声和叫卖声，但到了院子里就被墙挡住了，只剩下一点隐隐约约的嗡嗡声。几只麻雀落在枣树的枝头上，歪着脑袋看了看他，又飞走了。
他站了片刻，然后出了门。
content_en:
Chapter 45 Yunzhou
The walls of Yunzhou City appear gray in the afternoon light. They are neither high nor short. Some places on the city wall have cracked, and clumps of dead grass have grown out of the gaps, swaying in the wind.
In front of the city gate, there was a line of people waiting to enter the city - there were sellers carrying burdens, farmers driving donkey carts, and a few merchants leading horses. They were scattered in twos and threes, blocking the city gate and slowly moving forward. The seller's load was filled with needlework and cloth, the farmer's cart was piled with bundles of dry firewood, and the merchant's horse was loaded with bulging baggage. A soldier guarding the city squatted next to a donkey cart, turned over the bundles of firewood on the cart, and waved his hand to let the cart pass.
Su Chen led the horse and stood at the end of the queue. After waiting for a while, it was finally his turn.
Four soldiers were guarding the city gate. One was sitting on a bench collecting entry fees, two were standing watching people, and one was looking through the documents of those entering the city. When it was Su Chen's turn, he handed over the documents for entering the city.
The city guard soldier took it and took a look - his eyes paused on a mark on the corner of the document. Without saying anything, he closed the document and handed it back to him.
"Excuse me, please wait a moment." He said, turned around and walked a few steps towards the city gate.
He whispered something to a soldier next to him. The soldier nodded and hurried to the city.
Su Chen stood by the city gate and waited for a while. The team behind him was still moving forward slowly. Someone glanced at him and then shrank back. No one knew what he was waiting for. He leaned on the saddle, holding the reins with one hand, and his eyes fell on the people coming and going in the city gate, with no expression on his face.
Not long after, a middle-aged man wearing gray cloth and short brown clothes walked quickly out of the city.
He did not wear official uniform and looked like a steward, but he walked neatly and his steps were fast and steady. His eyes quickly scanned the crowd and locked onto Su Chen - he didn't hesitate or look around, as if he already knew what Su Chen looked like and where he was standing.
He came over, cupped his hands and whispered: "Master, follow me."
He didn't call him Prince, and without any unnecessary words, he turned around and led the way.
Su Chen led the horse and followed him.
The two men crossed two streets. There were gradually more and more people on the street - a vendor carrying a load pushed past them, with bamboo baskets hanging on both ends containing vegetables and tofu. Some people were squatting on the roadside picking a pile of mountain products and bargaining with the stall owners. A child ran after a dog and almost hit Su Chen's horse. Su Chen pulled the reins and made the horse avoid it.
He turned into a quiet alley and stopped in front of a side door. The man knocked on the door twice, and the door opened from the inside. He turned sideways to let Su Chen in, then stayed outside the door without following him.
There was already a butler-looking person waiting inside the door. The housekeeper was about fifty years old, wearing a gray cloth gown that had been washed white, and his hair was combed meticulously. He didn't say much, just bowed slightly, and then led Su Chen through a corridor to the entrance of the main hall.
Not long after, a middle-aged man wearing a blue official uniform walked out quickly.
He was about in his early forties, with a fair complexion and a neatly trimmed short beard on his chin. When he saw Su Chen, he smiled and cupped his hands.
"I am Xu Jingtang, the Chief Minister of Yunzhou. You must be the Crown Prince - the prince mentioned in his letter that I have been waiting at the door for a while."
He said, turning sideways and saying, "Please come in quickly."
Su Chen also cupped his hands, called "Lord Simu", and followed him into the house.
The main hall is not big, but it is well kept. There is a calligraphy hanging on the wall opposite the gate - it says "Still water runs deep", written with a steady hand. There are two rows of dark wood chairs on both sides, and a coffee table in the middle with a celadon tea set on it. The window opened to the south, and the afternoon light shone in from the window, casting a bright square grid on the floor tiles.
Xu Jingtang led him to the main seat, sat down, and personallyAfter pouring the tea, Ping retreated to the left and right.
He waited until the footsteps were far away before he spoke.
"The prince sent someone to fly over a few days ago and said that the prince was going south to Tianyi on errands and would stop by Yunzhou." Xu Jingtang smiled. "The letter also said to let me take care of him."
He picked up the tea bowl and took a sip, his eyes falling on Su Chen.
"How many days does the prince plan to stay in Yunzhou?"
"We will leave after one night's rest and continue our journey early tomorrow morning." Su Chen said. "Don't dare to bother Sir Mu too much."
"What's the trouble?" Xu Jingtang waved his hand. "It's rare for the prince to ask me to do anything. Since the prince is here, he can stay here with peace of mind. The place in the mansion is spacious, I will ask someone to prepare a guest room."
Su Chen paused.
"Thank you Sir Simu for your kindness." Su Chen said. "But there are many people coming and going in the house, and I don't feel comfortable living there. If it's convenient for Sir Simu, just help me arrange a quiet place to live in the city. There's no need to be too particular."
Xu Jingtang glanced at him without forcing himself, and nodded with a smile.
"That's okay. There is an empty courtyard on East Street. It's usually unoccupied. I'll have someone clean it up. The prince can live there. If you are free in the evening, can you come over for a quick meal?"
Su Chen said "Hello".
After sitting for a while, Xu Jingtang asked a few questions about the situation on the road - how many days we had been walking, whether the road was good, and whether it was peaceful along the way. I asked a few more questions about the current situation in Shuozhou - how is the prince's health, how is the princess, and how is the situation at the border. They all talked about common things, and the tone was casual, as if they were chatting with the son of an old friend. Su Chen answered one by one. He didn't say much, but he didn't feel alienated either.
After chatting a few more words, Su Chen stood up and left.
Xu Jingtang asked the housekeeper who had just led the way to take Su Chen to the courtyard on East Street.
The yard is not big. The layout as soon as you enter has two main rooms and one wing room. The middle of the yard is paved with blue bricks, and a jujube tree is planted in the corner. The leaves have almost fallen off. A few dead leaves were still hanging on the branches, swaying twice when the wind blew, but they never fell. There are a few thin weeds growing in the cracks between the bricks under the tree. They have dried up and a small bunch of yellow-brown trees are huddled in the corner.
It was fairly clean and the bedding was new. There wasn't much furniture in the room, but it had everything it needed - a bed, a table, a chair, and a washstand standing in the corner. The window paper was newly pasted, and the light coming in was soft and even. There was a faint soapy smell in the air, as if it had just been cleaned.
Su Chen put down his luggage, washed his face, and stood in the yard for a while.
The branches of the jujube trees intertwined overhead, cutting the gray sky into tiny pieces. The wind blew in from the entrance of the courtyard, carrying the faint sounds of people and hawkers coming from the street, but when it reached the courtyard it was blocked by the wall, leaving only a faint buzzing sound. A few sparrows landed on the branches of the jujube tree, looked at him with their heads tilted, and then flew away.
He stood for a moment and then walked out the door.
